subject: Banking
title: Blockchain in Banking
description: A quick win: understand Blockchain in Banking.

hook.text: JPMorgan processes $1 billion daily on its blockchain platform Onyx. Banks are using the technology they once dismissed.

buildup.text: Blockchain enables instant settlement, transparent record-keeping, and smart contracts that execute automatically.

discovery.text: Cross-border payments that take 3-5 days through SWIFT can settle in seconds on blockchain.

twist.text: Banks want private blockchains they control. The decentralization crypto advocates love is what banks want to avoid.

climax.text: Banks adopted blockchain's technology but rejected its philosophy.

punchline.text: Banks use blockchain now. But they want control, not decentralization.

quiz.question: How do banks use blockchain differently than crypto advocates intended?
options: Banks use private, centralized blockchains instead of decentralized ones

details.summary: Traditional banks are exploring blockchain for cross-border payments, trade finance, and settlement, attracted by its promise of faster, cheaper transactions but cautious about integration with legacy systems and regulation.
details.whyItMatters: Blockchain could eliminate the slow, expensive correspondent banking system that currently takes days and charges high fees for international transfers, potentially saving the global economy billions annually.
takeaways: JPMorgan created its own blockchain platform called Onyx
Cross-border payments are the most promising use case for banks
Most bank blockchain projects remain in pilot phase after years

faq.question: Why are banks interested in blockchain if they opposed crypto?
faq.answer: Banks distinguish between public cryptocurrencies that bypass them and private blockchains they control. Bank blockchain projects use the distributed ledger technology while maintaining institutional control over access and governance.

faq.question: Has any bank successfully deployed blockchain at scale?
faq.answer: JPMorgan's Onyx processes over $1 billion daily in transactions. HSBC has settled over $3 trillion in foreign exchange trades using blockchain. However, most bank blockchain projects remain limited in scope compared to traditional systems.
